item.title: Deprecation Notice
item.description:
Overview

Watchtower has a number of legacy notification configuration options that will be removed with the release of Watchtower v2.

This deprecation and eventual removal of legacy notification configuration options is a long-term migration that started with the refactoring of Shoutrrr into a separate notification library. The removal of the legacy notification configuration options is simply a removal of an unnecessary abstraction layer in favor of using Shoutrrr URL’s directly.

In order to continue receiving notifications, users will need to add Shoutrrr URL’s directly using the NOTIFICATION URL configuration option.

Watchtower users do not need to install any new software to implement Shoutrrr URL’s.

Use Watchtower’s CLI migration tool to help convert legacy email configurations to Shoutrrr URLs or use the Shoutrrr Playground to help convert configurations for other services to Shoutrrr URLs.

General Options

  • watchtower-notifications

Email Notifications

  • notification-email-from
  • notification-email-to
  • notification-email-server
  • notification-email-server-tls-skip-verify
  • notification-email-server-user
  • notification-email-server-password
  • notification-email-subjecttag
  • notification-email-server-port
  • notification-email-delay

Gotify Notifications

  • notification-gotify-url
  • notification-gotify-token
  • notification-gotify-tls-skip-verify

Microsoft Teams Notifications

  • notification-msteams-hook

Slack Notifications

  • notification-slack-hook-url
  • notification-slack-identifier
  • notification-slack-channel
  • notification-slack-icon-emoji
  • notification-slack-icon-url

item.title: Migration Tool
item.description:
Overview

Watchtower includes a notify-upgrade command to help convert legacy notification configurations to Shoutrrr URLs for use with the NOTIFICATION URL.

It parses legacy Watchtower notification configurations and outputs Shoutrrr URLs to a temporary file inside the Watchtower container.

Settings the file leaves out The file holds only the notification URL. It leaves out two legacy email settings, which are not part of a Shoutrrr URL. Watchtower applies both while your legacy settings are in place. When you switch to the generated URL, set their replacements yourself:

  • notification-email-delay is replaced by notifications-delay.
  • notification-email-subjecttag is replaced by notification-title-tag.

Usage

The notify-upgrade command converts legacy Watchtower notification configurations into Shoutrrr URLs and writes them to a temporary file inside the container.

Running the Command

The notify-upgrade can be run either against a Watchtower container that is already running or as a single-run instance that allows you to convert a Docker Compose configuration or Docker CLI flag / environment variable configuration.

Existing Deployment

If Watchtower is already deployed and running with your legacy notification configuration, you can execute notify-upgrade directly inside the container:

docker exec watchtower /watchtower notify-upgrade

This works because the Watchtower binary is installed at /watchtower and notify-upgrade is a built-in subcommand. The common mistake is running docker exec watchtower notify-upgrade, which fails because notify-upgrade is not a standalone executable in $PATH.

Running notify-upgrade inside an existing container does not stop or restart the main Watchtower process. docker exec runs a separate, short-lived process. The only side effect is that the notify-upgrade process will stay alive for up to 5 minutes while waiting for you to retrieve the temporary file, after which it cleans up and exits.

Single-Use Run

If you have not yet deployed Watchtower or if you want to run notify-upgrade as a one-off command without starting the persistent Watchtower update loop, then run a temporary container configured with notify-upgrade as the command.

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 command: notify-upgrade
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: smtp.example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT: 587
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER: USERNAME
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD: 'PASSWORD'
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=smtp.example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=587 \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER=USERNAME \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD='PASSWORD' \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade \
 --notifications email \
 --notification-email-server smtp.example.com \
 --notification-email-server-port 587 \
 --notification-email-server-user USERNAME \
 --notification-email-server-password 'PASSWORD' \
 --notification-email-from sender@example.com \
 --notification-email-to recipient@example.com

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server. notify-upgrade writes an @ in it as %40.
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, inside the single quotes. In a Compose file, write each ' in it as '' and each $ as $$. In a shell command, write each ' as '\''.

Use your SMTP server’s host name in place of smtp.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 command: notify-upgrade
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: gotify
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL: "https://gotify.example.com/"
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN: "TOKEN"
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY: true
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=gotify \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_URL="https://gotify.example.com/" \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TOKEN="TOKEN" \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_GOTIFY_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade \
 --notifications gotify \
 --notification-gotify-url "https://gotify.example.com/" \
 --notification-gotify-token "TOKEN" \
 --notification-gotify-tls-skip-verify

Replace TOKEN with the application token from your Gotify server and gotify.example.com with your server’s host name.

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 command: notify-upgrade
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: slack
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SLACK_HOOK_URL: "https://hooks.slack.com/services/WORKSPACE_ID/WEBHOOK_ID/WEBHOOK_TOKEN"
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SLACK_IDENTIFIER: watchtower-server-1
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=slack \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SLACK_HOOK_URL="https://hooks.slack.com/services/WORKSPACE_ID/WEBHOOK_ID/WEBHOOK_TOKEN" \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_SLACK_IDENTIFIER=watchtower-server-1 \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade \
 --notifications slack \
 --notification-slack-hook-url "https://hooks.slack.com/services/WORKSPACE_ID/WEBHOOK_ID/WEBHOOK_TOKEN" \
 --notification-slack-identifier watchtower-server-1

Replace the following with the parts of your Slack webhook URL:

  • WORKSPACE_ID: the workspace ID, which starts with T
  • WEBHOOK_ID: the webhook ID, which starts with B
  • WEBHOOK_TOKEN: the webhook token
services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 command: notify-upgrade
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: msteams
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_MSTEAMS_HOOK_URL: "https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE"
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=msteams \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_MSTEAMS_HOOK_URL="https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE" \
 nickfedor/watchtower \

docker run --rm \
 --name watchtower-notify-upgrade \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 notify-upgrade \
 --notifications msteams \
 --notification-msteams-hook "https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE"

Replace the following with the parts of the webhook URL that your workflow’s trigger shows:

  • ENVIRONMENT: the Power Platform environment
  • WORKFLOW_ID: the workflow ID
  • SIGNATURE: the value of the sig parameter

An Azure Logic Apps workflow’s URL has a different form. Use the whole URL that its trigger shows.

Replace the example environment variables with your own legacy notification configuration. The notify-upgrade command inspects the container’s current configuration, so it must be started with your legacy notification settings.

Retrieving the Generated File

After running notify-upgrade, the converted Shoutrrr URL is written to a temporary file in the container’s working directory. Its name starts with watchtower-notif-urls- and ends in a random number.

The command logs a copy command with the container and the file name:

INFO To get the environment file, use: docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env

This output includes the following values:

  • CONTAINER_ID: the ID of the container that ran notify-upgrade. When notify-upgrade cannot find its own container ID, the line shows <CONTAINER> instead. Replace it with the container’s name or ID before you run the command, because a shell reads < and > as redirections.
  • FILE_NAME: the name of the temporary file, such as watchtower-notif-urls-1234567890

Run that command to copy the file to your local machine:

docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env

The temporary file is automatically removed after 5 minutes or when the container stops, so copy it promptly after generation. If you are running notify-upgrade as a one-off command (docker run --rm ...), the process will wait up to 5 minutes before exiting. Before it writes the file, notify-upgrade checks every URL with Shoutrrr, as Watchtower does at startup. If Shoutrrr rejects a URL, such as a Discord webhook whose ID is not a number, notify-upgrade writes no file. Its error never contains the URL. It usually names the service. It cannot when the URL has no scheme or does not parse. The same holds for a URL that ends in an empty # fragment. The error gives a notification URL’s position, counting from 1. For a URL converted from a legacy notification type, it names that type instead. Shoutrrr’s warnings about a URL, such as a deprecated key, appear in the log. When the conversion fails, notify-upgrade logs the error and exits with code 1. It removes any file it started to write. If it logs “Failed to remove temporary file” instead, delete the file named in that warning yourself, because it can hold your notification credentials.

Migration Walkthrough

Select the tab that matches your legacy notification service.

1. Run the following Docker Compose configuration / Docker CLI command:

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: smtp.example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT: 587
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER: USERNAME
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD: 'PASSWORD'
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY: 10
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECTTAG: Watchtower
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run -d \
--name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=smtp.example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=587 \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER=USERNAME \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD='PASSWORD' \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY=10 \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SUBJECTTAG=Watchtower \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notifications email \
 --notification-email-server smtp.example.com \
 --notification-email-server-port 587 \
 --notification-email-server-user USERNAME \
 --notification-email-server-password 'PASSWORD' \
 --notification-email-from sender@example.com \
 --notification-email-to recipient@example.com \
 --notification-email-delay 10 \
 --notification-email-subjecttag Watchtower

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server. notify-upgrade writes an @ in it as %40.
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, inside the single quotes. In a Compose file, write each ' in it as '' and each $ as $$. In a shell command, write each ' as '\''.

Use your SMTP server’s host name in place of smtp.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.

2. With the container running, execute the notify-upgrade command:

docker exec watchtower /watchtower notify-upgrade

Then copy the resulting file out of the container with the command that notify-upgrade logs:

docker cp CONTAINER_ID:FILE_NAME ./watchtower-notifications.env

3. The following converted Shoutrrr URL should be produced:

smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s

4. Replace the deprecated configuration with the converted Shoutrrr URL. The URL does not carry the email delay or the subject tag. Set the notifications delay and the title tag in their place:

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: 'smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s'
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_DELAY: "10"
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TITLE_TAG: Watchtower
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e 'WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL=smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s' \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS_DELAY=10 \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_TITLE_TAG=Watchtower \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notification-url 'smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?auth=Plain&clienthost=localhost&encryption=Auto&fromaddress=sender%40example.com&fromname=Watchtower&subject=&toaddresses=recipient%40example.com&usehtml=No&usestarttls=Yes&timeout=10s' \
 --notifications-delay 10 \
 --notification-title-tag Watchtower
The single quotes keep YAML and the shell from changing the URL. `notify-upgrade` writes a `'` in the password as `%27` but leaves a `$` as it is. In a Compose file, write each `$` in the URL as `$$`.
  • Avoid using unrecognized flags like WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_SSL, as they are ignored and may cause confusion.
  • Use the encryption and usestarttls URL parameters in the smtp:// URL to control TLS behavior rather than deprecated flags.

 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL="teams:?color=%23406170&host=https%3A%2F%2FENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com%3A443%2Fpowerautomate%2Fautomations%2Fdirect%2Fworkflows%2FWORKFLOW_ID%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Fpaths%2Finvoke%3Fapi-version%3D1%26sp%3D%252Ftriggers%252Fmanual%252Frun%26sv%3D1.0%26sig%3DSIGNATURE" \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notification-url "teams:?color=%23406170&host=https%3A%2F%2FENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com%3A443%2Fpowerautomate%2Fautomations%2Fdirect%2Fworkflows%2FWORKFLOW_ID%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Fpaths%2Finvoke%3Fapi-version%3D1%26sp%3D%252Ftriggers%252Fmanual%252Frun%26sv%3D1.0%26sig%3DSIGNATURE"

Automated Migration Script

If you have a docker-compose.yaml with a watchtower service configured for legacy notifications, you can use the script below to run the entire migration process end-to-end. It starts the container, executes notify-upgrade, extracts the generated file, prints its contents, and cleans up.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SERVICE="${1:-watchtower}"
OUTPUT="${2:-./watchtower-notifications.env}"

CONTAINER=$(docker compose run -d "${SERVICE}" notify-upgrade)

trap 'docker rm -f "${CONTAINER}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT

if ! docker ps -q --filter "id=${CONTAINER}" | grep -q .; then
 echo "notify-upgrade container exited before producing output. Logs:" >&2
 docker logs "${CONTAINER}" >&2 || true

 exit 1
fi

FILE=""
TIMEOUT=300
INTERVAL=2
ELAPSED=0

while [[ ${ELAPSED} -lt ${TIMEOUT} ]]; do
 FILE=$(docker logs "${CONTAINER}" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'watchtower-notif-urls-[^ ]+' | tail -1 || true)

 if [[ -n "${FILE}" ]]; then
 break
 fi

 sleep "${INTERVAL}"

 ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + INTERVAL))
done

if [[ -z "${FILE}" ]]; then
 echo "Timed out waiting for notify-upgrade output. Logs:" >&2
 docker logs "${CONTAINER}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

 exit 1
fi

docker cp "${CONTAINER}:${FILE}" "${OUTPUT}"

echo "=== Generated Shoutrrr URL ==="
cat "${OUTPUT}"
  • The service must already be defined in docker-compose.yaml with your legacy notification environment variables. The script assumes the service name defaults to watchtower.
  • The command will self-cleanup after 5 minutes or when the script exits.
  • notify-upgrade keeps a Slack channel only when it is a Slack channel ID, such as C0123456789. A channel name such as #ops or a user such as @dana cannot be carried into the Shoutrrr URL, so the generated URL uses the webhook’s own channel and notify-upgrade logs a warning. Webhooks created by a Slack app always post to their own channel.

item.title: Email Notifications
item.description:
Deprecated Email Notification Options

The following legacy email notification options are deprecated and subject to removal with the release of Watchtower v2:

  • notification-email-from
  • notification-email-to
  • notification-email-server
  • notification-email-server-tls-skip-verify
  • notification-email-server-user
  • notification-email-server-password
  • notification-email-subjecttag
  • notification-email-server-port
  • notification-email-delay

Use the notification-url configuration option with a smtp:// Shoutrrr URL instead.

Use the legacy notifications migration tool to help with migrating to a Shoutrrr URL.

Overview

Watchtower uses Shoutrrr’s SMTP service to send email notifications.

Examples 

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?fromaddress=sender@example.com&toaddresses=recipient@example.com
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL="smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?fromaddress=sender@example.com&toaddresses=recipient@example.com" \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notification-url "smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:587/?fromaddress=sender@example.com&toaddresses=recipient@example.com"

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server, with an @ in it written as %40
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, percent-encoded

Use your SMTP server’s host name in place of smtp.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.

/// details | The following legacy SMTP configuration examples are deprecated and will be removed with the release of Watchtower v2. type: warning

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: smtp.example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT: 587
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER: USERNAME
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD: 'PASSWORD'
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY: 10
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: email
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM: sender@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO: recipient@example.com
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER: relay.example.com
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

This example sends through an SMTP relay at relay.example.com that accepts mail on port 25 without authentication.

If the relay offers STARTTLS, Watchtower checks its certificate against the server name, so the certificate must be valid for relay.example.com. A relay in the same Compose project can take that name as a network alias.

docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=smtp.example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=587 \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_USER=USERNAME \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER_PASSWORD='PASSWORD' \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_DELAY=10 \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notifications email \
 --notification-email-from sender@example.com \
 --notification-email-to recipient@example.com \
 --notification-email-server smtp.example.com \
 --notification-email-server-port 587 \
 --notification-email-server-user USERNAME \
 --notification-email-server-password 'PASSWORD' \
 --notification-email-delay 10
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=email \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_FROM=sender@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_TO=recipient@example.com \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SERVER=relay.example.com \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notifications email \
 --notification-email-from sender@example.com \
 --notification-email-to recipient@example.com \
 --notification-email-server relay.example.com

These examples send through an SMTP relay at relay.example.com that accepts mail on port 25 without authentication.

If the relay offers STARTTLS, Watchtower checks its certificate against the server name, so the certificate must be valid for relay.example.com.

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, inside the single quotes. In a Compose file, write each ' in it as '' and each $ as $$. In a shell command, write each ' as '\''.

Use your SMTP server’s or relay’s host name in place of smtp.example.com or relay.example.com and your own addresses in place of sender@example.com and recipient@example.com.

///

Common SMTP Configurations

Property Value
Port 587
Authentication OAuth2 client credentials
RequireStartTLS Yes 
smtp://GMAIL_USER%40gmail.com:APP_PASSWORD@smtp.gmail.com:587/?fromaddress=GMAIL_USER%40gmail.com&toaddresses=TO_ADDRESS&encryption=ExplicitTLS&usestarttls=yes&timeout=30s

Replace the following:

  • GMAIL_USER: the part of your Gmail address before the @
  • APP_PASSWORD: your Gmail password, or an App Password
  • TO_ADDRESS: the address that receives the notifications, with its @ written as %40

For Gmail, use an App Password if two-factor authentication is enabled.

Omit spaces from the App Password. Google displays the 16-character passcode in groups of four, but those spaces are not part of the password.

Do not use &auth=OAuth2 with an App Password. That method expects a SASL XOAUTH2 access token in the password field.

Property Value
Port 587
Authentication OAuth2 client credentials
RequireStartTLS Yes 
smtp://SMTP_USERNAME:SMTP_PASSWORD@email-smtp.REGION.amazonaws.com:587/?fromaddress=FROM_ADDRESS&toaddresses=TO_ADDRESS&encryption=ExplicitTLS&usestarttls=yes&timeout=30s

Replace the following:

  • SMTP_USERNAME: the user name of your Amazon SES SMTP credentials
  • SMTP_PASSWORD: the password of your Amazon SES SMTP credentials, percent-encoded
  • REGION: the AWS Region of your Amazon SES endpoint, such as us-east-1
  • FROM_ADDRESS: a verified sender address, with its @ written as %40
  • TO_ADDRESS: the address that receives the notifications, with its @ written as %40
Property Value
Port 587
Authentication OAuth2 client credentials
RequireStartTLS Yes 
smtp://MAILBOX@smtp.office365.com:587/?fromaddress=FROM_ADDRESS&toaddresses=TO_ADDRESS&clientid=CLIENT_ID&clientsecret=CLIENT_SECRET&scopes=https%3A%2F%2Foutlook.office365.com%2F.default&tokenurl=https%3A%2F%2Flogin.microsoftonline.com%2FTENANT_ID%2Foauth2%2Fv2.0%2Ftoken&requirestarttls=yes&timeout=30s

Replace the following:

  • MAILBOX: the address of the sending mailbox, with its @ written as %40
  • FROM_ADDRESS: the sender address, with its @ written as %40
  • TO_ADDRESS: the address that receives the notifications, with its @ written as %40
  • CLIENT_ID: the application (client) ID of your app registration
  • CLIENT_SECRET: the client secret of your app registration, percent-encoded
  • TENANT_ID: your Microsoft Entra tenant ID

Shoutrrr gets OAuth2 access tokens from Microsoft Entra ID with the client credentials grant. Follow Shoutrrr’s Microsoft 365 guide to register the application and give it access to the sending mailbox.

Exchange Online turns off Basic authentication for SMTP AUTH by default in existing tenants at the end of December 2026. A URL with a password, such as smtp://MAILBOX:PASSWORD@smtp.office365.com:587/, works only while the tenant allows it.

Property Value
Port 465
Encryption ImplicitTLS
UseStartTLS No 
smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:465/?fromaddress=FROM_ADDRESS&toaddresses=TO_ADDRESS&encryption=ImplicitTLS&usestarttls=no&timeout=30s

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server, with an @ in it written as %40
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, percent-encoded
  • FROM_ADDRESS: the sender address, with its @ written as %40
  • TO_ADDRESS: the address that receives the notifications, with its @ written as %40
Property Value
Port 25
Encryption None
UseStartTLS No 
smtp://USERNAME:PASSWORD@smtp.example.com:25/?fromaddress=FROM_ADDRESS&toaddresses=TO_ADDRESS&encryption=None&usestarttls=no&timeout=30s

Replace the following:

  • USERNAME: the user name for your SMTP server, with an @ in it written as %40
  • PASSWORD: the password for your SMTP server, percent-encoded
  • FROM_ADDRESS: the sender address, with its @ written as %40
  • TO_ADDRESS: the address that receives the notifications, with its @ written as %40

Notes

  • Timeout:

    • The default SMTP timeout is 10 seconds.
    • If you experience timeouts (e.g., failed to send: timed out: using smtp), add &timeout=30s to the URL to allow more time for server responses, especially with proxies or slow networks.

  • Authentication:

    • Use &auth=Plain for username and password authentication, including Gmail App Passwords. This is the default when credentials are provided.
    • Set clientid, clientsecret, scopes and tokenurl to have Shoutrrr get OAuth2 access tokens with the client credentials grant, as the Microsoft 365 example does. Shoutrrr then uses OAuth2 without &auth=OAuth2.
    • Use &auth=OAuth2 only for SASL XOAUTH2 with a static access token in the password field. App Passwords are not OAuth2.

  • Testing:

    • Install Shoutrrr using one of the various installation methods.

    • Test your URL with the Shoutrrr CLI:

      shoutrrr send -u "NOTIFICATION_URL" -m "Test message"

      Replace NOTIFICATION_URL with the smtp:// URL to test.

  • Proxy Issues:

    • If using a Docker proxy (e.g., tcp://dockerproxy:2375), ensure it allows outbound connections to your SMTP server’s host and port.
    • Test connectivity with telnet SMTP_HOST SMTP_PORT inside the container. Replace SMTP_HOST with your SMTP server’s host name and SMTP_PORT with its port.

Overview

Examples 

services:

  • notification-slack-hook-url
  • notification-slack-identifier

Use the notification-url configuration option with a slack:// Shoutrrr URL instead.

Overview

Watchtower can use Shoutrrr’s Slack service to send Slack notifications.

Examples 

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:

Replace the following with the parts of your Slack webhook URL, https://hooks.slack.com/services/WORKSPACE_ID/WEBHOOK_ID/WEBHOOK_TOKEN:

  • WORKSPACE_ID: the workspace ID, which starts with T
  • WEBHOOK_ID: the webhook ID, which starts with B

services:

item.title: Microsoft Teams Notifications
item.description:
Deprecated Teams Notification Option

The following legacy Teams notification option is deprecated and subject to removal with the release of Watchtower v2:

  • notification-msteams-hook

Use the notification-url configuration option with a teams:// Shoutrrr URL instead.

Overview

Watchtower can use Shoutrrr’s Teams service to send Microsoft Teams notifications.

The webhook URL comes from a Power Automate workflow with the “When a Teams webhook request is received” trigger or from an Azure Logic Apps workflow. In Power Automate, set the trigger’s “Who can trigger the flow?” option to “Anyone”. Watchtower sends with the URL’s sig signature and cannot sign in to your tenant. Copy the whole URL from the trigger.

Watchtower checks the webhook URL at startup through Shoutrrr, whether it is set in a teams:// URL or in the legacy option. It must use https:// and carry a sig signature. Its host must be one that Microsoft issues for workflows. Watchtower refuses to start with any other URL, such as a retired Office 365 connector URL on webhook.office.com. Shoutrrr’s webhook URL rules list the accepted hosts.

Power Automate URLs on logic.azure.com Power Automate flows left logic.azure.com on November 30, 2025. Their old URLs on that domain no longer trigger them. Copy the current URL from the flow’s trigger.

Watchtower still accepts logic.azure.com URLs because Azure Logic Apps workflows use that domain.

Examples

In a teams:// URL, the host value is the whole webhook URL, percent-encoded as in the examples below. Encode its percent signs too, so %2F becomes %252F. A raw & would end the host value early. The legacy option takes the webhook URL unencoded.

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_URL: "teams://?host=https%3A%2F%2FENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com%3A443%2Fpowerautomate%2Fautomations%2Fdirect%2Fworkflows%2FWORKFLOW_ID%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Fpaths%2Finvoke%3Fapi-version%3D1%26sp%3D%252Ftriggers%252Fmanual%252Frun%26sv%3D1.0%26sig%3DSIGNATURE&title=Alert"
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notification-url "teams://?host=https%3A%2F%2FENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com%3A443%2Fpowerautomate%2Fautomations%2Fdirect%2Fworkflows%2FWORKFLOW_ID%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Fpaths%2Finvoke%3Fapi-version%3D1%26sp%3D%252Ftriggers%252Fmanual%252Frun%26sv%3D1.0%26sig%3DSIGNATURE&title=Alert"

Replace the following with the parts of the webhook URL that your workflow’s trigger shows:

  • ENVIRONMENT: the Power Platform environment
  • WORKFLOW_ID: the workflow ID
  • SIGNATURE: the value of the sig parameter

An Azure Logic Apps workflow’s URL has a different form. Use the whole URL that its trigger shows, percent-encoded for the host value.

/// details | The following legacy Microsoft Teams examples are deprecated and will be removed with the release of Watchtower v2. type: warning

services:
 watchtower:
 image: nickfedor/watchtower:latest
 environment:
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS: msteams
 WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_MSTEAMS_HOOK_URL: "https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE"
 volumes:
 - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATIONS=msteams \
 -e WATCHTOWER_NOTIFICATION_MSTEAMS_HOOK_URL="https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE" \
 nickfedor/watchtower
docker run -d \
 --name watchtower \
 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
 nickfedor/watchtower \
 --notifications msteams \
 --notification-msteams-hook "https://ENVIRONMENT.environment.api.powerplatform.com:443/powerautomate/automations/direct/workflows/WORKFLOW_ID/triggers/manual/paths/invoke?api-version=1&sp=%2Ftriggers%2Fmanual%2Frun&sv=1.0&sig=SIGNATURE"

///
